shape_hint: Cylindrical-threaded plug: a short hexagon head (height m) sitting on a round collar (diameter dk, thickness c) that has a flat/undercut seat for a sealing ring (DIN 7603), below which a short fully threaded cylindrical shank of length i is used. Overall length h = i + c + m. No drive recess; the plug is turned by an external hex of width across flats s.

role_map.dk_max: collar diameter d2, max = nominal (tol h14)
role_map.m: hex head height above the collar (nominal, +-1/2 IT15)
role_map.s: hex width across flats (DIN 475-1 value where the standard lists one, else ISO 272)

notes: Metric fine-pitch sizes only (Form A cylindrical thread, DIN 13-x / ISO 965). Pitch shown is the finest series pitch; M20, M30, M36, M42, M45, M48, M52 are also available in P=2 with the same other dimensions. Two sources (ISO 272 values M16 16, M18 16, M20 18, M22 18, M24 21) show a smaller across-flats than DIN 475-1; the table keeps the DIN 475-1 value (17,17,19,19,22), which is what distributors stock. Dissenting cells found on the older German shop dataset (theo-schrauben.de / schrauben-lexikon.de / wegertseder.com, all identical): M18 m=6, M38 c=4, M45 dk=55, M48 s=36 - overruled by >=3 independent sources, and monotonic checks. Pipe-thread (G 1/8 A .. G 2 A) variants exist and are not in this table. Stainless/steel/brass use the same dimensions; DIN 910 is used with DIN 7603 sealing rings (see sealw). Chinese standards-database pages (globalfastener.com, partscad.com, 164580.com) carry the same numbers as Fuller in the same layout; treated as copies of Fuller, not counted.

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched all 5 listed URLs live (HTTP 200) and parsed tables with Python. 19 rows x 8 cols (152 cells) matrix vs Fuller (10 transposed tables, 3 cols each), torqbolt table 0, ssfast, Ganter (d2,l1=i,l3=m,sw=s), theo/lexikon. Clusters agreeing per column (min over rows): P 4, c 3, dk_max 3, i 3, h 3, m 4, s 4. h is supported only by Fuller (h approx), torqbolt ((lt) approx) and ssfast (l approx) - Ganter has no overall length (l2=c+m only, not counted). s checked per row: M10=10, M12=13, M14=13 (Fuller/torqbolt DIN 475-1 column is '-', ISO 272 column gives 10/13/13); M16..M24=17,17,19,19,22 (DIN 475-1 column; ISO 272 column = 16,16,18,18,21); M26..M56 = 24,24,24,27,27,27,30,30,30,30,36 (DIN 475-1 '-', ISO 272 value). ssfast, Ganter (sw) and theo (s) print the same unlabelled series for every row they carry, so each s cell has 4-5 clusters. Physical: h=i+c+m all 19 rows, all columns non-decreasing, dk>s.
problems: s column mixes series by construction: DIN 475-1 value where the standard prints one (M16-M24), otherwise the single ISO 272 value (DIN 475-1 column is '-', i.e. identical). Per-row values are right and multi-source; label must say 'wrench size per DIN 475-1' and must not be read as ISO 272 (alt for M16-M24 would be 16,16,18,18,21).

h has exactly 3 clusters; it only passes if Fuller and torqbolt count as independent. Evidence for independence: different layout (Fuller transposed with computed min/max rows; torqbolt row table with kw/mass), different footnote markers ('16^' vs '16d'), no shared typo (Fuller header 'M63' for M64; torqbolt has none). If lead rules them one cluster, h fails for all rows (and c M38 / dk M45 drop to 2).
German shop dataset typos (not counted): M18 m=6, M38 c=4, M45x1.5 dk=55 (its own M45x2 row says 52), M48x1.5 s=36.

P: M20,M30,M36,M42,M45,M48,M52 also exist as x2 with identical dimensions; record lists the finer pitch only. Ganter lists M42/M48 only as x2 (not counted for P). Row key is d only, so P is not a unique key.
